papers.title: One night of sleep deprivation reduces spatially patterned human brain clearance: implications for simulated tau propagation
papers.abstract: Neurotoxic protein fragments such as amyloid-beta and tau accumulate in characteristic staging patterns in Alzheimer's disease. The brain clears such substances via multiple systems, including the extracellular-extravascular route known as glymphatic clearance, but how such clearance is distributed across the brain, how this distribution is affected by sleep, and its implications for neurodegenerative disease progression remain unclear. Using Bayesian inference to fit a kinetic model of enhancement and clearance to longitudinal CSF tracer-enhanced MRI, we estimate CSF tracer clearance rates for every connectome region in 21 subjects. We find that clearance is spatially patterned across the living human brain and consistent between subjects. Clearance rates are amongst the highest in the entorhinal cortex and decrease across regions in Braak stage order. One night of sleep deprivation reduces mean clearance levels while leaving the spatial pattern largely unchanged. To study how mean clearance level and spatial pattern affect tau propagation in silico, we use the CSF tracer clearance rates as a proxy for regional tau clearance in a computational model of protein accumulation, spread, and regional damage. Across subject-specific simulations, clearance level and spatial pattern have distinct effects on tau propagation. The clearance level determines the timescale of simulated pathology, while the spatial pattern shapes its accumulation and onset. These results identify CSF tracer clearance as a spatially organised property of the human brain that is reduced by sleep deprivation, and suggest that its overall level and regional organisation may independently shape the timing and spatial progression of neurodegenerative proteinopathy.

ai.reason: Directly examines effects of sleep deprivation on brain clearance using longitudinal imaging and computational modeling, highly relevant to sleep homeostasis and recovery mechanisms.
ai.summary: Using Bayesian inference on CSF tracer-enhanced MRI in 21 subjects, the study estimated region-specific brain clearance rates that were spatially patterned and highest in entorhinal cortex, decreasing in Braak stage order. One night of sleep deprivation reduced mean clearance while preserving the spatial pattern, and computational simulations showed that clearance level sets tau propagation timescale while spatial pattern shapes accumulation and onset.

papers.title: Symptoms of anxiety are linked to N3 sleep and lower dissipation of slow-wave activity during nocturnal sleep.
papers.abstract: Slow-wave sleep (SWS) is vital for brain health, memory, and emotional resilience. Slow-wave activity (SWA) reflects homeostatic sleep pressure, which dissipates across successive sleep cycles. Impaired SWA dissipation has been linked to depression. We examined whether reduced SWA dissipation is associated with symptoms of anxiety and depression in healthy conscripts. Seventy conscripts (67 males, aged 18-24) undergoing compulsory military service participated in overnight polysomnography. SWA dissipation was assessed by comparing normalized delta (0.5-4.0 Hz) electroencephalogram power between first and third NREM sleep episodes. This was complemented by full spectral analysis of sleep stages. Psychological measures included Overall Anxiety Severity and Impairment Scale, Beck's Depression Inventory, and Epworth Sleepiness Scale. Conscripts with elevated anxiety (24%) exhibited weaker SWA dissipation and greater proportion of N3 sleep. Similarly, anxiety was negatively correlated with SWA dissipation and positively with proportion of N3. Additionally, conscripts with elevated anxiety but without elevated depressiveness had less REM sleep than those with both anxiety and depression, as well as those without symptoms. Findings related to sleepiness or depression without anxiety were limited. In full spectral analysis individuals with higher anxiety exhibited elevated alpha power during REM sleep, potentially reflecting cortical hyperarousal. Higher proportion of N3 sleep and lower SWA dissipation were associated with greater anxiety rather than depression. These findings highlight the importance of adequate SWS in emotion regulation. Impaired SWA dissipation may contribute to preservation of negative emotional memories during sleep. Another possibility is that hyperarousal increases need for recovery sleep.

Higher anxiety also correlated with elevated alpha power during REM sleep, suggesting cortical hyperarousal.

papers.title: Inhibition of Cerebellar Dentate Nucleus-Zona Incerta Glutamatergic Circuit Improves Sleep Disturbances in Chronic Temporal Lobe Epilepsy Model.
papers.abstract: Patients with chronic temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) frequently experience various sleep disorders, characterized by reduced sleep duration, diminished sleep stages, and disrupted sleep patterns. Recent research has identified a population of GABAergic neurons in the ventral zona incerta (ZI) that is instrumental in promoting sleep, along with a neural pathway that connects the cerebellar dentate nucleus (CDN) to the ZI. However, the precise role of this circuit in regulating sleep patterns remains inadequately understood. This study employed anatomical, chemogenetic, optogenetic, and immunofluorescence staining techniques to investigate the potential of the CDN-ZI circuit in ameliorating sleep disturbances associated with TLE. Our findings indicate that pilocarpine-treated mice exhibit significant sleep fragmentation and reduced sleep duration, particularly during non-rapid eye movement sleep. By employing optogenetic and chemogenetic methods to target CDN glutamatergic neurons, we observed a decrease in sleep fragmentation, an increase in overall sleep duration, and an enhancement in sleep quality in pilocarpine-treated mice. The inhibition of the CDN-ZI glutamatergic circuit through optogenetic and chemogenetic methods resulted in substantial improvements in sleep disturbances following TLE. Targeting the CDN-ZI glutamatergic circuit represents a promising therapeutic strategy for addressing sleep disorders resulting from chronic TLE.

ai.summary: Using optogenetic and chemogenetic inhibition of the cerebellar dentate nucleus-zona incerta glutamatergic circuit in a pilocarpine mouse model of chronic temporal lobe epilepsy, the study found reduced sleep fragmentation, increased sleep duration, and improved sleep quality. The authors propose targeting this circuit as a therapeutic strategy for TLE-associated sleep disturbances.

papers.title: Enhanced local synchronization with impaired large-scale recruitment of NREM slow waves in pediatric disorders of arousal
papers.abstract: NREM slow waves emerge from the synchronization of neuronal activity across multiple spatial scales. During childhood, local synchronization and large-scale propagation undergo distinct maturational trajectories, paralleling cortical synaptic remodeling and the maturation of long-range brain connectivity. How alterations in this local-to-global organization relate to arousal instability remains poorly understood. Here, we used 256-channel high-density EEG to characterize NREM oscillatory organization in 17 children with disorders of arousal (DOA) and 17 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Children with DOA showed a marked dissociation between local synchronization and large-scale coordination: slow waves were locally larger, steeper and more synchronized, yet recruited the cortex less globally and exhibited a more spatially restricted distribution of origins. This phenotype preferentially involved Type 1 slow waves, a subtype associated with widespread cortical and subcortico-cortical recruitment and late developmental maturation. Children with DOA also showed reduced centro-posterior slow spindle density, providing convergent evidence for altered coordination of distributed NREM oscillations. These microstructural abnormalities occurred despite largely preserved conventional sleep architecture. Together, our findings reveal an altered local-to-global organization of NREM sleep in pediatric DOA and suggest that vulnerability to incomplete arousals may emerge when strong local synchronization is not matched by effective large-scale network coordination during brain development.

They also had reduced centro-posterior slow spindle density, indicating altered NREM oscillation coordination despite preserved conventional sleep architecture.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm maturation in infancy: a large-scale analysis of sleep-wake pattern development from 3 to 18 months based on longitudinal data.
papers.abstract: Infant sleep-wake rhythms consolidate rapidly during the first year, yet normative trajectories and their variability remain poorly characterized. We examined sleep-wake development between 3 and 18 months using prospective, event-level data from a large international cohort. Sleep logs from 175,593 infants (10.7 million logged days) were collected via a mobile tracking application. Parents recorded each sleep event prospectively. We analyzed developmental changes in daytime sleep and nap frequency, compensation during nap transitions, bedtime stability as a circadian marker, relationships between sleep timing and need, and rank-order stability of individual differences. Total sleep decreased from 14.8 h at 3 months to 12.5 h at 18 months, reflected almost entirely by reductions in daytime sleep (226 to 101 min) as nap frequency declined from 3.9 to 1.0 per day. During the early nap transitions, the remaining naps lengthened to compensate for 88-89% of the sleep time lost when a nap was dropped. Compensation was lower during the transition from two naps to one nap (79%). Within-infant bedtime variability decreased most steeply before 9 months, consistent with circadian consolidation. Individual differences in bedtime regularity were highly stable across age periods (Spearman r = 0.73-0.77). Infants with greater sleep need had earlier bedtimes and more daytime sleep, while daytime sleep and time in bed were negatively correlated (r = -0.48). The decline in total sleep across infancy results from reductions in daytime sleep through fewer and eventually shorter naps. Bedtime regularity increases most rapidly before 9 months, and individual differences emerge early and persist, suggesting enduring circadian traits are already established in infancy. Substantial inter-individual variability underscores the importance of individually tailored guidance.

ai.summary: A large-scale longitudinal analysis of sleep logs from 175,593 infants found that total sleep decreased from 14.8 h at 3 months to 12.5 h at 18 months, driven by reduced daytime sleep as nap frequency declined from 3.9 to 1.0 per day. Bedtime regularity increased most steeply before 9 months, and individual differences in bedtime regularity were highly stable across age periods.

papers.title: A brain circuit linking sleep loss to pain.
papers.abstract: Sleep loss heightens pain sensitivity, but the brain circuits involved remain unclear. In a recent study, Huang, Wang, Jiao, and colleagues identified a pathway connecting the retrosplenial cortex, anterior cingulate cortex, and zona incerta that contributes to heightened sensitivity to mechanical stimulation and heat after sleep deprivation in male mice.

ai.summary: This commentary discusses a study identifying a retrosplenial cortex–anterior cingulate cortex–zona incerta circuit that contributes to heightened mechanical and heat sensitivity after sleep deprivation in male mice, highlighting a specific brain pathway linking sleep loss to pain.

papers.title: Disease progression shapes circadian and locomotor disruption in a model of multiple sclerosis
papers.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of the central nervous system featuring a wide range of debilitating symptoms. Wearable activity recording devices have recently been adopted to improve symptom monitoring in MS, capturing symptoms related to sleep/wake cycles, circadian disruption, and fatigue. However, comparable measures of activity have yet been established in pre-clinical models of MS, the most widely used being experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE). We therefore sought to characterize changes in continual home-cage activity over the course of EAE, and establish whether home-cage monitoring can be used as an observer-independent measure of disease progression. Our results showed that locomotor activity in the mid-active/dark phase was most severely affected by EAE. Disrupted circadian (24-hour) activity was observed during the peak and onset stages of disease. Bout activity analysis revealed >40-minute long activity bouts as a sensitive indicator of non-motor symptoms independent of clinical score-based motor deficits. Current assessment of disease progression in EAE relies on clinical scores, which primarily assess motor deficits through visual observation prone to observer bias. Various computed activity parameters were found to be altered during key disease stages, suggesting that a combination of activity measures can serve as objective indicators of disease progression. Overall, our results show that home-cage activity effectively captures signs of non-motor symptoms in the EAE model of MS and can serve as an observer-independent measure of EAE disease progression.

Mid-active/dark-phase locomotor activity was most affected; circadian disruption occurred at onset and peak, and >40-minute activity bouts detected non-motor symptoms independently of clinical motor scores.

papers.title: Recombinant bovine αs1-casein ameliorates PCPA-induced insomnia-like behavioral and physiological abnormalities in mice.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is a multifactorial sleep-wake disorder associated with altered neurotransmitter homeostasis, systemic inflammatory changes, and gut microbial dysbiosis. Recombinant bovine αs1-casein (RC) is a scalable milk-protein ingredient, but its effects on insomnia-like physiological and behavioral abnormalities have not been systematically evaluated. We investigated RC in a p-chlorophenylalanine (PCPA)-induced mouse model. Male ICR mice received RC (100, 300, or 500 mg kg-1 day-1), melatonin, Naoxinshu oral liquid, natural casein, or vehicle for 7 days after PCPA modeling. Body weight, open-field behavior, serum cytokines, brain neurotransmitters, hippocampal histology, organ indices, and cecal microbiota were assessed. RC improved body-weight recovery and open-field performance without altering major-organ indices. It increased brain 5-HT, 5-HIAA, dopamine, GABA, and glutamate concentrations and reduced the elevated norepinephrine concentration. High-dose RC reduced serum IL-6 and was associated with better-preserved hippocampal morphology. 16S rRNA gene sequencing showed RC-associated changes in bacterial richness and community structure. The parallel physiological, neurochemical, inflammatory, and microbial changes support an association between RC administration and improvement of PCPA-induced insomnia-like abnormalities. These results identify recombinant bovine αs1-casein as a promising food-derived ingredient for further investigation in sleep-health applications, while the microbiota-gut-brain axis is presented as a testable mechanistic framework rather than a demonstrated causal pathway.

RC improved body-weight recovery and open-field performance, increased brain 5-HT, 5-HIAA, dopamine, GABA, and glutamate, reduced elevated norepinephrine, lowered IL-6 at high dose, and was associated with altered bacterial richness and community structure.

papers.title: Circadian timing does not modulate human temporal contrast sensitivity.
papers.abstract: Previous studies have reported diurnal variations in color perception and luminance contrast sensitivity, suggesting modulation of visual processing by the circadian pacemaker. To clarify potential time-of-day effects, we examined whether cone-mediated temporal contrast sensitivity is modulated by circadian timing. We disentangled circadian and homeostatic influences on human visual performance using a 40-hour forced desynchrony protocol. Twelve participants (five female participants, 24.4 ± 2.9 years, range 19-30) followed a repeating 3.75-hour cycle comprising 2 hours 30 minutes of wakefulness and 1 hour 15 minutes of sleep under constant environmental conditions. Circadian period was estimated from up to 46 salivary melatonin samples per participant. During wake periods, participants repeatedly completed temporal contrast sensitivity tasks at 2 Hz and 8 Hz, using tasks that probed both luminance (L+M+S) and chromatic (L-M, S-cone-directed) modulations. We tested for circadian modulation of visual performance by comparing hierarchical cosinor models with intercept-only null models using Bayes factors. All participants showed robust melatonin rhythms (mean τ = 24.18 ± 0.39 hours). Bayesian inference provided decisive evidence against circadian variation in luminance or chromatic contrast sensitivity. Within this controlled protocol, we found no detectable near-24-hour modulation of cone-mediated temporal contrast sensitivity. Previously reported time-of-day effects may instead reflect homeostatic influences, pupil-linked changes in retinal illuminance, or mechanisms outside the cone-mediated pathways probed here. By separating circadian phase from sleep-wake-related influences, this study clarifies when circadian modulation of visual performance can and cannot be inferred.

The results suggest that previously reported time-of-day effects may reflect homeostatic or non-circadian factors.

papers.title: AMPK-dependent brain-wide norepinephrine release promotes recovery from metabolic coma in mice
papers.abstract: Coma is a pathological brain state characterized by loss of consciousness. How the brain recovers from coma remains largely unknown. Using mouse models of metabolic coma, we identified an endogenous neuromodulatory pathway that actively promotes coma recovery. In mice subjected to hypoglycemic coma, hypoglycemia triggered AMPK-dependent excitation of nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS) neurons, which activated locus coeruleus (LC) norepinephrine neurons through a glutamatergic NTS-LC circuit. LC activation drives widespread norepinephrine release across cortical and subcortical regions, thereby promoting post-coma arousal. Notably, coma-associated brain-wide norepinephrine release was unconventional in both scale and duration, with a magnitude approximately 10-fold higher than physiological norepinephrine release during sleep-wake cycles. This neuromodulatory process also operated during hypercapnic coma. Vagus nerve stimulation accelerated coma recovery by engaging this endogenous anti-coma mechanism. Our findings uncover an AMPK-dependent brainstem circuit that actively restores arousal from metabolic coma, revealing a neural defense strategy against profound metabolic stress.

ai.summary: In mouse models of metabolic coma, hypoglycemia triggered AMPK-dependent excitation of nucleus tractus solitarius neurons that activated locus coeruleus norepinephrine neurons via a glutamatergic circuit. This drove brain-wide norepinephrine release at ~10-fold higher magnitude than physiological sleep-wake release and promoted arousal, with vagus nerve stimulation accelerating recovery.

papers.title: Sleep-related Brain Activity in an Arousal-reducing Agent-induced Mouse Model Evaluated with fMRI.
papers.abstract: Functional MRI (fMRI) has been established as a technique for capturing functional changes based on brain activity and is widely used to evaluate various diseases and physiological conditions. However, studies that systematically evaluate functional brain networks during arousal-reducing agent-induced sleep in mice by using resting-state fMRI (rsfMRI) are limited. This study aimed to compare and analyze whole-brain functional connectivity (FC) and reorganization patterns of large-scale brain functional networks in the mouse brain during arousal-reducing agent-induced sleep, focusing on arousal-reducing agents acting on different arousal regulatory systems. Sixteen healthy male C57BL/6JmsSlc mice (aged 16.4 ± 8.7 week) were used in this study. The mice were assigned to 4 groups: control, zolpidem (20 mg/kg), lemborexant (40 mg/kg), and dexmedetomidine (75 μg/kg). rsfMRI was performed using a 9.4T MRI system equipped with an 86 mm volume transmit coil and an 8-channel receive-only coil (Bruker BioSpin, Ettlingen, Baden-Württemberg, Germany). After head post-surgery and habituation, blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) images were acquired using a gradient-echo echo-planar imaging (GRE-EPI) sequence (TR/TE = 1500/14 ms). Each mouse underwent six 10 min imaging sessions. fMRI data were preprocessed using Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM12; Wellcome Centre for Human Neuroimaging, London, UK) and analyzed using the CONN FC toolbox (McGovern Institute for Brain Research, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA, USA). ROI × ROI FC matrices were calculated for each fMRI session. Group differences were assessed using linear mixed-effects models that accounted for repeated measurements within animals, individual variability, and age differences among groups. Compared to the control group, the zolpidem group showed the smallest overall differences, whereas the dexmedetomidine group showed the largest differences. Furthermore, although relatively similar trends were observed between the groups in the distribution of mean correlation coefficients within each network, different trends were observed between the networks. In addition to network reorganization associated with the sleep-inducing state, which is commonly observed regardless of the arousal-reducing agent type, distinct network changes exhibiting arousal-reducing agent-specific connectivity patterns were observed.

papers.title: Investigating the transfer of physical stimuli to the dreamed body: A comparative study of muscular, vestibular, and haptic stimulation on dream incorporation.
papers.abstract: The relationship between the dreamed body and the physical body remains an open question in sleep and dream research. This study examined whether somatosensory stimulation applied during REM sleep modulates the corresponding dream content under controlled conditions. Using a within-subject design, we compared three stimulation modalities-electrical muscular, galvanic vestibular, and haptic vibration-each paired with a modality-specific sham stimulation. Twenty-four participants completed one adaptation night followed by three consecutive experimental nights in the sleep laboratory. Dream reports were collected following rapid eye movement sleep awakenings after stimulation or sham periods, yielding a total of 120 reports. Dream incorporation of bodily sensations and actions was observed across all conditions; however, generalized linear mixed-effects analyses revealed no statistically significant differences between stimulation and sham conditions for any modality. No evidence for reliable modality-specific dream incorporation was observed under rigorous sham-controlled conditions. Rather than demonstrating robust stimulation-specific effects, these findings suggest that contextual and expectancy-related influences substantially contribute to bodily dream content under laboratory conditions while highlighting methodological challenges in dream incorporation research. By combining multiple somatosensory stimulation modalities with rigorous sham-controlled procedures, the present study provides a methodological benchmark for future investigations of dream incorporation and dream engineering.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Chronic Intermittent Hypoxia Induces Persistent Venous Narrowing of Downstream Parenchymal Microvessels and Pial Veins in the Male Mouse Cortex.
papers.abstract: Chronic intermittent hypoxia (IH), a hallmark of sleep apnea, can lead to cerebral hypoperfusion and cognitive decline, though its precise impact on cerebral microcirculation remains unclear. This study investigated the longitudinal effects of 2-week chronic IH (8% O2, 6.5-min cycle for 6 hours/day) on brain microcirculation in the male mouse cortex. We observed a significant reduction in the diameters of pial veins (from 55 to 46 μm) and parenchymal venules (from 9.9 to 8.2 μm) after chronic IH relative to pre-IH conditions, while upstream arteries (47 to 44 μm) and arterioles (12.4 to 12.0 μm) were unaffected. This selective reduction in downstream venule diameter led to a significant increase in arterio-venous transit time, indicating reduced cerebral blood perfusion. Furthermore, neurovascular coupling (NVC) responses showed a substantial decrease, pointing to impaired microvascular function. Crucially, these neurovascular impairments were reversed by daily administration of an endothelin receptor antagonist during IH exposure, with the exception of pial vein constriction. In conclusion, reduced cerebral perfusion after chronic IH is associated with persistent narrowing of parenchymal venules and pial veins. These findings provide new insights into the cerebral microvascular complications of chronic IH and suggest the potential utility of neurovascular protective agents.

papers.title: Frontal theta power prospectively associated with response inhibition.
papers.abstract: A proactive mechanism has been postulated to promote successful inhibition. Specifically, this mechanism is thought to operate before any action-demanding or countermanding event has occurred. In the current study, we investigated whether theta-range oscillatory power measured using electroencephalography (EEG) could reflect this mechanism in a sample of healthy individuals performing a stop-signal task. We tested whether frontal-midline (FM) theta power preceding failed versus successful stop trials predicts inhibition success. Results from two experiments demonstrate that FM theta is indeed higher preceding successful stopping events than failed ones. However, theta power turned out to be equally stronger preceding slow than fast, go trials, suggesting that proactive slowing could explain the association between theta and stop success. There was no correlation between the strength of the within-subject theta-stop-success association and the within-subject theta-RT association. In sum, group-average-level analysis suggests strong overlap between FM theta associated with proactive inhibition and proactive slowing, respectively, while at the same time there are dissociations in terms of individual differences. A further, unexpected, finding was that FM alpha power was specifically associated with proactive inhibition but not with slowing, and, relative to theta, peaked closer in time to the action-demanding event.

FM theta was higher before successful stopping than failed stopping, but was also stronger before slow versus fast go trials, and FM alpha was specifically associated with proactive inhibition rather than slowing.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation Selectively Alters Cellular Stress Responses During Exercise in the Heat in Young and Older Males.
papers.abstract: Older adults are at heightened risk of heat-related morbidity, particularly in occupational settings where insufficient sleep and heat exposure commonly coincide. Autophagy and other proteostatic pathways are essential for maintaining cellular homeostasis during acute physiological stress; however, whether acute sleep deprivation modifies these responses during exercise-heat stress remains unknown. Ten young (23±3 years) and 10 older (61±4 years) males completed an exercise-heat stress test following normal sleep and after 24 h of total sleep deprivation in which participants performed three 30-min cycling bouts at fixed rates of metabolic heat production (150, 200, and 250 W·m -2), each separated by 15 min rest in the heat (40°C, ~13% relative humidity). Autophagy and related cellular stress pathways were assessed before and after exercise. Sleep deprivation did not alter macroautophagy-related proteins, including LC3-II, the LC3-II/I ratio, ULK1 phosphorylation, or beclin-2 in either age group. However, p62 was reduced at end-exercise in young males following sleep deprivation (p=0.010), whereas the corresponding reduction in older males did not reach statistical significance. Sleep deprivation differentially altered proteins involved in chaperone-mediated autophagy, with LAMP-2A decreasing in young males but increasing in older males (both, p≤0.004). In older males, sleep deprivation reduced HSP90 and increased cleaved-caspase-3 and TNF-α (both, p≤0.048), indicating greater apoptotic and inflammatory signaling. Our findings indicate that 24 h of sleep deprivation does not broadly alter markers of macroautophagy during exercise-heat stress but selectively modifies cellular stress pathways in older males, with distinct responses observed in young and older males.

papers.title: Machine Learning Framework for Integration of Video and EEG Reveals Distinct Seizure Phenotypes in Mouse Models of Epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Video-electrocorticogram (VEEG) recordings are the gold-standard diagnostic tool for detecting and characterizing seizures in rodent models of seizure and epilepsy. Manual/visual scoring remains the prevailing strategy despite significant limitations. Alternatively, automated and semi-automated analyses have been applied to either EEG or video features alone but integrating these disparate data forms presents a challenge that has not been sufficiently addressed. Here, we introduce an integrated machine learning pipeline that jointly leverages EEG and behavioral video data to enable scalable and objective event classification. Integrated video-EEG analysis was initially validated using a well-established pharmacologically induced seizure paradigm in male mice, where overt generalized motor seizures provide a clear benchmark. We then tested the pipeline on a genetic mouse model of developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) that displays a complex spike-wave discharge (SWD) seizure phenotype that poses significant challenges for traditional scoring methods. Machine learning-powered integrated analysis of video-EEG recordings outperformed unimodal EEG- or video-based approaches and performed favorably to experienced rodent EEG electrophysiologists while also uncovering distinct phenotypic relationships, including classes of atypical behavioral and typical non-behavioral SWD events. This framework provides a flexible tool for high-throughput, precise analysis of VEEG data, with potential to accelerate discovery in epilepsy and seizure research. Furthermore, this approach represents a generalizable strategy for the integration of diverse neurobehavioral time series data types.Significance Statement Seizure detection in animal models of epilepsy has relied heavily on manual analysis of video-EEG recordings, a process that is slow and subjective. We present a machine learning pipeline that integrates EEG and video data from mice to classify seizures with high accuracy. This work was validated across two models, first a pharmacologically induced generalized seizure model, and second, a spontaneous spike-wave discharge (SWD) model in genetic epilepsy. Our approach detected events missed by human reviewers and revealed previously uncharacterized SWD subtypes distinguished by their behavior. By combining open-source tools in a flexible framework, this work lowers the barrier to high-throughput, unbiased seizure phenotyping, and also offers a broadly applicable strategy for linking neural activity to behavior in neuroscience research.

papers.title: Associations Between Resting-State EEG Delta-band Activity at Selected Parietal Electrodes and Cognitive Changes Following Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in Patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment: An Exploratory Analysis.
papers.abstract: Transcutaneous auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation (taVNS) may improve cognition in Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), but its electrophysiological correlates remain unclear. We explored whether parietal delta-band changes were associated with cognitive changes following taVNS. This exploratory secondary analysis included 26 participants with MCI from a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial (taVNS, n = 14; sham, n = 12) who had valid resting-state EEG data at baseline and Week 24. Absolute and relative 1-3 Hz delta power at Pz, P1, P2, and P5 were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA and EEG-cognitive correlations with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. Absolute delta power showed significant time effects at all four electrodes after FDR correction (all q = 0.008). Relative delta power at Pz showed an uncorrected group effect (F = 5.007, p = 0.035; q = 0.218). papers.title: Frustrative nonreward engages midfrontal theta power and modulates effort expenditure.
papers.abstract: Irritability is characterized by a propensity to experience frustration and has been associated with reduced self-reported willingness to expend effort for rewards. Frustration may be relevant to effortful reward pursuit, but its effects on effort expenditure have rarely been experimentally tested in humans. To address this gap, this study introduced a frustration induction in the Effort-Doors task to elicit frustrative nonreward (FNR), a negative emotional state triggered by unexpected reward loss, and examined its effects on physical effort expenditure and feedback-related electroencephalographic (EEG) activity. We also tested whether these effects vary as a function of state and trait measures of motivation and affect. Linear mixed-effects models tested the effects of FNR induction on self-reported, behavioral, and EEG measures in young adults (N = 83) completing the Frustrative Effort-Doors task. Models tested manipulation effects, trial-level post-feedback adjustment, and moderation by state and trait measures. Midfrontal theta power (MFθ) extracted using multivariate spatial filtering was examined as a function of feedback (win vs. FNR), effort (low vs. high), and subsequent behavioral adjustments. The frustration condition was associated with decreased self-reported state motivation and increased frustration, arousal, and response speed. Midfrontal theta power was larger following FNR feedback and increased with state frustration during high-effort trials. Higher state frustration was associated with reduced response vigor during effort execution following FNR feedback. MFθ did not predict trial-to-trial behavioral adjustments. These findings indicate that FNR recruits MFθ, a neural marker of cognitive control, while state frustration modulates physical effort execution following unexpected reward loss.

papers.title: Chronotherapeutic and Circadian Rhythm-Based Strategies in Diabetes Management: A Critical Opinion Based on Evidences.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is one of the world's leading health problems, and standard approaches to therapy do not take into consideration the impact of circadian misalignment on metabolic health. Chronobiological processes are involved in regulating glucose homeostasis, insulin release, hepatic glucose production, lipids, and energy metabolism; hence, disruptions such as those caused by non-rhythmic sleep patterns, shifts at work, irregular meal times, and light exposure could cause insulin resistance and even type 2 diabetes. The current critical review discusses the light-melatonin interaction and personalized chronobiological medicine. Instead of giving a descriptive account of particular treatments, the paper introduces the integrative importance of chronobiology for the management of diabetes by considering data about chrononutrition, time-restricted feeding, chronopharmacology, chrono-exercise, and an approach to chronometabolism based on the integration of the timing of meals, drugs, exercise, sleep, and light exposure with chronotype, metabolic phenotype, and the feasibility of the therapy. Circadian timing can be a promising adjuvant in the treatment of diabetes; however, the available evidence does not suggest an ideal time for intervention. Further studies should focus on measuring time, well-powered randomized controlled trials, long-term outcomes, and individualization of chronotherapy.

papers.title: In-laboratory polysomnography as the reference standard in sleep research: a bibliometric overview of human studies.
papers.abstract: In-laboratory attended Polysomnography (PSG) is the reference standard for objective sleep assessment. Although portable and wearable sleep technologies have advanced, the evolution of PSG research over the past decade has not been systematically characterized. Bibliometric data from the Web of Science Core Collection (2015-2025) were retrieved using a search strategy focused on in-laboratory, full-night PSG studies, yielding 462 publications for analysis. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and Microsoft Excel were used to conduct visual and quantitative analyses of publication trends, country- and institution-level co-authorship, journal distribution, author keywords, and keywords bursts. Annual publications exhibited a steady increase, with the United States and China as the leading contributors. Prominent institutions included Eindhoven University of Technology and Seoul National University. PSG research was predominantly published in specialized sleep medicine journals. Keyword analysis revealed a stable thematic core encompassing sleep monitoring, sleep staging, and sleep apnea, alongside emerging trends in machine learning, wearable devices, and brain modeling. Within the corpus of included in-laboratory PSG studies, research outputs demonstrated a sustained trajectory, exhibiting a pattern of parallel development between clinical applications and technical refinement. While PSG remains a foundational methodological pillar in this specific domain, its evolving integration with advanced computational methods underscores a continued commitment to bridging clinical relevance and technological progress within PSG-focused research.

papers.title: Night-to-night sleep variability and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality: a prospective cohort study with a complementary in vitro circadian-disruption experiment.
papers.abstract: Irregular sleep-wake patterns may disrupt circadian rhythms, but the dose-response relationship between night-to-night sleep variability and mortality and the association of sleep onset variability with death remain unclear. Using 4-7 valid days of wrist accelerometer data, including ≥1 weekend day, from 7,604 adults aged ≥20 years in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2011-2014, linked to mortality through December 2019, we examined the within-person SDs of sleep midpoint, sleep onset, and total sleep time across nights and the sleep regularity index (SRI) in relation to all-cause and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality. Survey-weighted Cox models were fitted across 20 imputed datasets and combined using Rubin's rules. Restricted cubic splines examined dose-response relationships. Complementary categorical, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses were conducted. Human umbilical vein endothelial cell (HUVEC) experiments repeated in three independent runs compared cellular responses under a regular dexamethasone schedule and four prespecified irregular schedule variants. Over a median follow-up of 81 months, 714 all-cause and 229 CVD deaths occurred. Each 1-hour increase in the across-night SD of sleep midpoint, sleep onset, and total sleep time was associated with all-cause mortality HRs of 1.22 (95% CI, 1.12-1.33), 1.19 (1.11-1.29), and 1.17 (1.05-1.31), respectively. The corresponding CVD mortality HRs were 1.21 (1.09-1.35), 1.22 (1.05-1.42), and 1.16 (0.94-1.42), respectively. Each 10-point lower SRI was associated with all-cause mortality (HR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.21-1.38) and CVD mortality (HR, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.18-1.45). Across three independent HUVEC runs, the mean response across the four prespecified irregular schedule variants showed lower core clock-gene expression, lower Griess assay absorbance, and higher inflammatory and adhesion-marker expression than the regular schedule. Greater night-to-night sleep irregularity was associated with higher hazards of all-cause and CVD mortality, although these associations were modest compared with those of older age, hypertension, and diabetes in the same models. The complementary cellular experiment showed differences between the regular dexamethasone schedule and the prespecified irregular schedule set.

papers.title: Association of Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) diet with sleep quality and quantity, inflammation and oxidative stress in Iranian adults: a cross-sectional study.

We evaluated the relation between MIND diet and sleep parameters in Iranian adults, taking biomarkers into account. A sample of 535 adults (46 % were female), with a mean age of 42·6 years, was selected via a multistage-cluster random sampling for this cross-sectional investigation. Dietary data were collected via a validated FFQ. Sleep quality and sleep duration were assessed by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index questionnaire. Concentration of biomarkers was assessed using participants' blood samples, taken after a period of night-fasting. In fully-adjusted model, participants in the highest (v. lowest) tertile of MIND diet had 54 % lower odds of short sleeping (ORT3v.T1 = 0·46, 95 % CI: 0·22-0·93), and subjects in the highest tertile of MIND score had 56 % lower odds of poor sleep quality (ORT3v.T1 = 0·44, 95 % CI: 0·21-0·95). These associations were stronger in participants with overweight and obesity. Higher adherence to MIND was associated with a lower probability of sleep disturbance (ORT3v.T1 = 0·27, 95 % CI: 0·08-0·89). There was no statistically significant association between the MIND diet and either oxidative stress or inflammatory biomarkers (P > 0·05). These findings highlighted inverse associations between higher MIND adherence and sleep disorders among Iranian adults. No significant associations between MIND adherence and biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress were found.

papers.title: Effectiveness of school-based sleep promotion programs for adolescents: a systematic review with meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: The objective of this review is to assess the effectiveness of school-based sleep promotion programs for adolescents on sleep knowledge, sleep hygiene, sleep quality, sleep behavior, sleep efficiency, health-related quality of life, and depressive or anxiety symptoms. Adolescence is a critical period for physical and mental development, during which, quality sleep is essential. However, many adolescents experience sleep deprivation due to factors such as excessive electronic device use, academic and peer pressures, stress, and anxiety. School-based sleep promotion programs have been proposed to address these issues, but their effectiveness remains unclear. This review included studies published in English, Spanish, and Portuguese that assessed the effectiveness of school-based sleep promotion programs for adolescents aged 10 to 19 years on sleep knowledge, sleep hygiene, sleep quality, sleep efficiency, sleep behavior, health-related quality of life, and depressive or anxiety symptoms. Both randomized controlled trials and quasi-experimental studies, with or without a comparator, were eligible. A comprehensive search strategy was used to identify relevant published and unpublished studies. Studies meeting the eligibility criteria were retrieved and their methodological quality was assessed by 2 independent reviewers using the JBI critical appraisal checklists for randomized controlled trials and quasi-experimental studies. Quantitative data were extracted using the standardized data extraction tool. Studies were pooled for statistical meta-analysis. Effect sizes were expressed as final post-intervention standardized mean differences, and their 95% CI were calculated. Heterogeneity was assessed statistically using the standard χ2 and I2 tests. Statistical analyses were performed using random-effects models and fixed-effect models. Where statistical pooling was not possible, the findings were presented in narrative format. A total of 34 studies met the inclusion criteria, with a total of 22,679 adolescents. Meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials showed statistically significant differences for sleep knowledge (SMD=0.99, 95% CI=0.48 to 1.50, P<0.001), sleep hygiene (SMD=-0.20, 95% CI=-0.31 to -0.09, P=0.0003), and depressive symptoms (SMD=-0.70, 95% CI=-1.12 to -0.29, P<0.001). No statistically significant differences were found for sleep quality (SMD=0.06, 95% CI=-0.16 to 0.27, P=0.62), sleep efficiency (SMD=0.12, 95% CI=-0.02 to 0.26, P=0.09), sleep behavior-total sleep time/sleep duration (SMD=0.69, 95% CI=-0.27 to 1.65, P=0.16), and sleep behavior-sleep onset latency (SMD=-0.88, 95% CI=-1.77 to 0.01, P=0.05). Large effect sizes were observed for sleep knowledge and sleep onset latency; moderate-to-large effects for depressive symptoms and total sleep time; and small effects for sleep hygiene, sleep efficiency, and sleep quality. The funnel plot for sleep knowledge did not suggest publication bias, and Egger's test was not statistically significant. These findings suggest that school-based sleep promotion programs can be effective in improving adolescents' sleep knowledge and sleep hygiene, and reduce depressive symptoms. However, the high variability in intervention designs and methodological quality highlights the need for further high-quality studies to identify the most effective components of these programs and clarify their long-term impacts. papers.title: Decoding user satisfaction during reading of pre-defined question-answer pairs: BCI approach using delta and gamma EEG.
papers.abstract: The rapid proliferation of large language models (LLMs) has intensified the need for robust evaluation frameworks to align artificial intelligence (AI) behavior with human expectations. While current reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) strategies heavily rely on explicit, post-hoc self-reports, these metrics are fundamentally limited by subjective biases and user non-compliance. To address this, the current study presents a novel brain-computer interface (BCI) framework that systematically characterizes the continuous, implicit neural correlates of user satisfaction and dissatisfaction during a reading-based evaluative task involving pre-validated LLM-generated question-answer pairs. Sixty-four-channel electroencephalography (EEG) data were recorded from 30 participants while they read and evaluated various LLM-generated responses. To capture genuine subjective experiences, individual trials were relabeled based on post-trial 5-point Likert scale ratings into five distinct evaluative states, and spatiotemporal spectral analyses were performed. A ShallowFBCSPNet architecture was further used to evaluate single-trial classification between the very satisfied and very dissatisfied conditions under a subject-mixed cross-validation scheme. Spatiotemporal spectral analyses revealed distinct neural oscillatory dynamics that temporally dissociate satisfaction and dissatisfaction. When reading highly satisfactory responses, a pronounced, sustained enhancement of low-frequency delta power was observed within the bilateral frontotemporal areas during the middle (4-8 s) and late (8-12 s) reading intervals, indexing high-order cognitive consolidation and reward processing. Conversely, processing highly dissatisfactory responses led to a localized suppression of high-frequency gamma power in the right frontotemporal region during the early interval (0-4 s), reflecting an immediate affective appraisal and expectation violation. Utilizing the ShallowFBCSPNet architecture, the system successfully discriminated between the "very satisfied" and "very dissatisfied" states, achieving an average accuracy of 81% under a subject-mixed cross-validation scheme. These findings demonstrate that user evaluative states are encoded via distinct frequency-specific cortical networks over differing temporal windows. By bridging cognitive neuroscience and artificial intelligence, this study establishes the conceptual and empirical foundation for passive BCI-driven implicit feedback channels, laying groundwork toward future real-time paradigms for next-generation LLM alignment; the classification result should be interpreted as a feasibility demonstration rather than an estimate of real-world decoding accuracy.

papers.title: Does chronic occupational demand alter EEG stress biomarkers during cognitive challenge? a study of emergency physicians.
papers.abstract: Acute cognitive challenge produces consistent changes in several EEG indices, including alpha-band desynchronization, frontocentral theta enhancement, beta-band activity, and the theta/beta ratio. These measures serve as common biomarkers of cognitive workload and stress. It is not yet clear whether chronic occupational exposure to high cognitive demand alters these responses. Emergency physicians offer a useful test case, since their work involves repeated cognitive control under time pressure and high-stakes decision-making. We recorded 19-channel electroencephalography from 17 board-certified emergency physicians and 18 non-healthcare comparison participants during eyes-open rest and a standardized composite challenge combining Stroop interference, serial subtraction, time pressure, and evaluative feedback. Spectral power was estimated with Welch's method, log-transformed, and analyzed using a hierarchical framework combining six a priori regional features with electrode-wise topographic mapping. Across groups, the challenge produced robust frontal and posterior alpha suppression and increased frontocentral theta, consistent with workload-related cortical engagement. No Group x Condition interaction survived false discovery rate correction for the regional features, and no exploratory electrode-wise interaction survived correction across the full feature set. A complementary Bayesian analysis yielded moderate evidence for the null for the alpha and theta features, but inconclusive evidence for the beta and theta/beta features. Sub-band decomposition showed the challenge-related beta increase was specific to high beta (20-30 Hz), while low and mid beta decreased in emergency physicians. These results indicate an absence of detectable large group differences in EEG stress biomarkers following prolonged occupational exposure to high cognitive demand, although the sample constrains this conclusion to large effects.

papers.title: Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Exploratory Pharmacodynamics of Melanin-Concentrating Hormone Receptor-1 Antagonist RGH-706 in Healthy and Overweight or Obese Men.
papers.abstract: This Phase 1 program evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and exploratory pharmacodynamics of the novel melanin-concentrating hormone receptor-1 antagonist RGH-706. Study A was a first-in-man, randomized trial comprising a double-blind, placebo-controlled single-ascending-dose part (0.1-162.5 mg) and a two-way crossover food-effect assessment at 62.5 mg in healthy men. Study B was a double-blind, placebo-controlled, single- and multiple-ascending-dose study in overweight or obese (otherwise healthy) men receiving a single dose followed by 14 days of once-daily dosing (2.5-22.5 mg/day). Safety assessments included clinical evaluations, ECGs and mood and sleep scales. RGH-706 concentrations in plasma and urine samples were measured by validated methods. Pharmacokinetics was characterized using non-compartmental analysis. Study B evaluated exploratory pharmacodynamic measures including appetite-related outcomes, food preference, test-meal food and macronutrient intake, body composition and metabolic biomarkers. In Study A (n = 68), systemic exposure increased approximately dose proportionally up to 62.5 mg and more than proportionally above, with tmax between 2.5 and 3.5 h and a bi-exponential disposition with a 29-35 h terminal half-life. Food ingestion had a negligible effect on exposure and renal clearance was also negligible. In Study B (n = 36), RGH-706 showed moderate accumulation with steady state reached within 8 days. Exploratory pharmacodynamic measures showed a trend towards lower total energy intake, preference for fatty foods and weight gain, primarily with the lower doses of 2.5 and 7.5 mg/day. RGH-706 was well tolerated across all doses and conditions in both studies. RGH-706 was safe, well tolerated and exhibited well-characterized pharmacokinetics. papers.abstract: To examine the longitudinal and nonlinear association between sleep duration and psychological frailty in middle-aged and older Chinese adults. Sensitivity analyses incorporated sleep measurements from 2013 and 2015, three-wave average sleep duration, sleep trajectories, and multiple imputation. We observed nonlinear associations, with estimated turning points at 7.56 h for nighttime sleep and 8.55 h for total sleep. Persistent short sleep was also associated with higher odds of psychological frailty (OR = 1.44, 95% CI: 1.15-1.81, p = 0.002). Multiple-imputation analyses yielded broadly similar estimates. Short nighttime sleep and persistent short sleep were associated with psychological frailty in middle-aged and older Chinese adults. These findings suggest that sleep duration may be relevant to psychological health although causal relationships remain to be established.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment preserves intestinal endocannabinoid signaling under LPS-inflammatory conditions.
papers.abstract: Environmental factors critically influence intestinal homeostasis, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. The endocannabinoid system (ECS), a key regulator of immune, metabolic, and epithelial functions, has emerged as a promising pharmacological target in inflammatory disorders. However, whether environmental context influences intestinal ECS signaling and the coordinated mechanisms underlying intestinal homeostasis during inflammation remains unclear. This study investigated the impact of environmental enrichment (EE) on intestinal ECS regulation in the context of impaired intestinal homeostasis during lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced systemic inflammation. Adult male mice were housed under standard or enriched conditions for four weeks before LPS challenge (830 μg/kg, i.p., 24 h). ECS receptors (Cnr1, Cnr2), ECS-related targets (Trpv1, Pparγ), metabolic enzymes (Nape-pld, Dagl-β, Faah, Magl), inflammatory mediators (Tlr4, Tnf-α, Il-6), epithelial barrier markers (Ocln, Zo-1), endocannabinoid levels (AEA and 2-AG), selected bacterial taxa, and microbiota-derived metabolites were evaluated in the proximal colon. LPS induced coordinated changes in the intestinal ECS-related measures, endocannabinoid levels, inflammatory signaling, barrier-associated markers, and the selected microbial-metabolic profile. EE mitigated several of these changes, including ECS-related transcriptional and protein alterations and local inflammatory responses, while modulating tight-junction proteins, selected fecal bacterial taxa, microbiota-derived metabolites, and the integrated multivariate profile. Overall, EE modulates intestinal response profile consistent with greater resilience to inflammatory stress across ECS, inflammatory, barrier-associated, and microbial-metabolic measures. These findings suggest that ECS regulation may represent a context-dependent determinant of responsiveness to ECS-targeting pharmacological interventions.

papers.title: Intermittent theta-burst stimulation versus sham stimulation for suicidal ideation and psychiatric symptoms in depressive disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: Suicidal ideation, depressive symptoms, anxiety, and sleep disturbance remain difficult to manage in psychiatric populations, and intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) has emerged as an accelerated, non-invasive neuromodulation strategy for these outcomes. This meta-analysis compares iTBS versus sham-iTBS across suicidal ideation, depression severity, anxiety severity, and sleep quality to guide clinical decision-making. We systematically searched relevant electronic databases in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Continuous outcomes were pooled as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals using random-effects inverse-variance models in RevMan 5.4. Heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 and χ 2 statistics, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. A p value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Six studies were included. iTBS significantly reduced suicidal ideation versus sham-iTBS (SMD = -0.51; 95% CI: -0.93 to -0.09; p = 0.02; I 2 = 70%; n = 181 vs. 157), and the effect remained significant with lower heterogeneity after exclusion of Qin et al. (p = 0.02; I 2 = 29%). Depression severity improved with iTBS (SMD = -1.06; 95% CI: -1.64 to -0.48; p = 0.0003; I 2 = 80%; n = 162 vs. 142), with heterogeneity decreasing to 24% after exclusion of Huang et al. Anxiety severity also improved (SMD = -0.68; 95% CI: -1.27 to -0.09; p = 0.02; I 2 = 79%; n = 139 vs. 120), and heterogeneity decreased to 38% after exclusion of Huang et al. Sleep quality did not differ significantly between groups (SMD = -0.32; 95% CI: -0.98 to 0.34; p = 0.35; I 2 = 67%; n = 75 vs. 49), based on two trials. iTBS was associated with a reduction in suicidal ideation compared with sham stimulation, but the small evidence base and between-study heterogeneity limit certainty. Secondary analyses suggested improvements in depression and anxiety severity, whereas sleep quality did not differ between groups. Larger, standardized randomized controlled trials with longer follow-up are needed to determine the magnitude and durability of any antisuicidal effect.

In addition, our corroborative study also uncovered that in ADHD subjects, theta and alpha waves are more dominant in the left hemispheric region, irrespective of the task state, and theta waves are notably prominent in the frontal region. papers.title: Paintable In Situ Gelling Bioelectronic Interfaces for Epidermal Electrophysiological Monitoring.
papers.abstract: Noninvasive epidermal electrophysiological monitoring is frequently constrained by unstable electrode-skin contact interfaces over soft, textured, and dynamically deforming skin. The predefined geometries of conventional electrodes limit their capacity to conform to local microtopography. Here, we introduce an in situ gelation strategy performed directly on the epidermis to construct a conformal ionic bioelectronic interface. A fluidic precursor comprising gelatin and tannic acid is initially stabilized against premature gelation via competitive solvent-solute interactions. Upon application, solvent evaporation and gelatin reassembly induce rapid network formation. This process directly yields a highly conformal and gently detachable interface with remarkably low contact impedance. The resulting hydrated dynamic network provides mechanical compliance, robust interfacial adhesion, stretch-tolerant ionic conduction, and cooling-induced interfacial weakening that enables gentle removal. papers.title: Association of Sleep Duration with MASLD Status and Hepatic Steatosis Index in Korean Adults: The Indirect Role of Sedentary Behavior.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects nearly three in ten adults globally, while its prevalence in South Korea has risen by approximately 3-4% per year. Although MASLD is linked to lifestyle factors, few studies have examined the associations among sleep duration, MASLD status, and the hepatic steatosis index (HSI). Accordingly, we evaluated the relationship between sleep duration and MASLD status and separately assessed whether sedentary behavior formed an indirect pathway between sleep duration and HSI, an indicator of hepatic steatosis. The analysis included 26,909 adults aged 20 years or older who participated in the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey from 2014 through 2021. Logistic regression was used to estimate the relationship of sleep duration with MASLD status. Mediation analysis was conducted using HSI as the outcome variable to examine whether sedentary behavior indirectly linked sleep duration with HSI. MASLD was identified in 23.2% of 26,909 participants. In the adjusted logistic model, MASLD odds were higher among participants sleeping ≤4 hours (OR = 1.44, 95% CI: 1.17-1.78) and those reporting ≥8 hours of sedentary time (OR = 1.17, 95% CI: 1.09-1.25). Correlations of HSI with sleep duration (r = -.06, p < .001) and sedentary behavior (r = .02, p < .001) were small. The mediation model yielded a direct association between sleep duration and HSI (β = -0.21, 95% CI: -0.26 to -0.16), whereas the indirect effect through sedentary behavior was statistically significant but minimal (β = -0.0073, 95% bootstrap CI: -0.0118 to -0.0032). MASLD status was related to both shorter sleep and longer sedentary time. Nevertheless, the very small correlations among sleep duration, sedentary behavior, and HSI offered little empirical support for a meaningful mediation pathway. Longitudinal research is required to establish the direction and timing of these relationships.

papers.title: Comprehensive Multimodal Diagnostics and Rehabilitation in Persistent Post-Concussion Syndrome Following Motor Vehicle Collision.
papers.abstract: Motor vehicle collisions (MVCs) are among the most common mechanisms of mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), and a meaningful proportion of affected individuals develop persistent post-concussion syndrome (PPCS) characterized by prolonged multidomain dysfunction. Conventional neuroimaging frequently fails to capture the underlying pathophysiology, leaving clinicians without objective diagnostic evidence. We describe a 57-year-old woman who sustained mTBI in a rear-end MVC in March 2023. Head computed tomography (CT) performed at the emergency department and a subsequent brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) were both unremarkable. Despite normal structural neuroimaging, comprehensive multimodal functional assessment identified functional abnormalities across eight domains: vestibular function (videonystagmography (VNG)), cortical electrophysiology (quantitative electroencephalography (qEEG)), pupillary autonomics (automated infrared pupillometry), postural stability (computerized dynamic posturography (CDP)), oculomotor control (saccadometry), cardiac autonomic regulation (24-h heart rate variability (HRV)), olfaction (University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT)), and computerized concussion assessment (C3 Logix). Standardized psychological assessments confirmed moderate depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) = 14), moderate anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) = 12), clinically significant post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms (PTSD Checklist for Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) (PCL-5 = 38)), and substantial headache impact (Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6) = 58). The patient underwent a 10-modality individualized rehabilitation program. Concussion Symptom Checklist (CSC) scores declined from 92 at initial presentation to 0 by July 2023 (17 weeks post-injury), with near-complete re-resolution to 8 by February 2024 following a transient stress-related exacerbation. When conventional neuroimaging is unremarkable, comprehensive multimodal functional testing may provide evidence consistent with mTBI pathophysiology and help guide targeted rehabilitation. This case illustrates the potential value of a systematic, multimodal approach in PPCS management, while acknowledging that definitive attribution of findings to the index injury is constrained by the single-case design and absence of a pre-injury functional baseline.

papers.title: Perceptions of Intra-Operative EEG Brain Monitoring During Pediatric Anesthesia Among Children and Parents: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Survey.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) monitoring during pediatric anesthesia may improve perioperative safety by optimizing anesthetic titration and reducing adverse outcomes. However, little is known about patient and caregiver perceptions regarding this technology and its implementation into routine anesthesia care. This study evaluates perceived importance, utility, and extent of reassurance provided by intra-operative EEG monitoring among pediatric patients and their parents. Secondary aims include identifying concerns surrounding general anesthesia (GA), concerns surrounding EEG monitoring, cost and willingness to pay, and sociodemographic and medical factors shaping these attitudes. We conducted an exploratory cross-sectional survey at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Singapore between July 2022 and September 2025. Respondents were parents of children aged 1-18 years and children aged 12-18 scheduled for elective procedures under general anesthesia. A 16-item anonymized questionnaire assessed perceptions of intra-operative EEG monitoring, concerns about anesthesia, and attitudes regarding the cost of EEG monitoring. Of 400 respondents (100 children, 300 parents), 83.5% rated intra-operative brain monitoring as "very" or "quite" important and 93% reported feeling more reassured by its use. Children were most concerned about intraoperative awareness and failure to awaken, whereas parents were most concerned about anesthetic side effects and dosage. Parents with higher education and whose children had prior anesthetic exposure reported greater reassurance from EEG monitoring. Cost was the leading concern regarding EEG monitoring, particularly among parents from families residing in public housing. Despite this, most parents (75%) and children (59%) expressed willingness to pay for EEG monitoring. Pediatric patients and parents viewed intra-operative EEG monitoring as important and reassuring, and expressed willingness to support its implementation despite cost concerns. These findings suggest that families are unlikely to be a major barrier to EEG adoption and highlight the need for clinician- and system-level strategies to integrate EEG monitoring into family-centered pediatric anesthesia care.

papers.title: Surgical Success in Obstructive Sleep Apnea Patients Using Preoperative Drug-Induced Sleep Endoscopy and Awake Endoscopy Considering Disease Severity.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a prevalent disorder characterized by recurrent episodes of airway obstruction during sleep, leading to fragmented sleep and oxygen desaturation. Identifying the precise site and pattern of obstruction is essential for surgical success. Awake endoscopy with Müller's maneuver (AEMM) has long been used, but drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) offers dynamic assessment under sleep-like conditions. To retrospectively compare surgical outcomes of OSA patients evaluated with DISE versus AEMM, stratified by disease severity, and to determine whether the comparative value of DISE over AEMM differs according to OSA severity as measured by AEMM (AHI). Records of 102 OSA patients undergoing sleep surgery between January 2022 and December 2024 at Hamad Medical Corporation were reviewed. Patients were grouped into AEMM-only (n = 54) and DISE (n = 48). Surgical success was defined as postoperative AHI < 15 events/hour and at least 50% reduction from baseline. Statistical analysis included independent and paired t-tests, chi-square tests, and the Johnson-Neyman procedure to identify AHI-based thresholds of DISE benefit. DISE group had higher surgical success compared to AEMM (62.5% vs. 40.7%, p = 0.114). Preoperative and postoperative AHI changes were significant in both groups (p < 0.001). Stratification revealed that moderate-to-severe OSA patients (AHI > 16.7) had significantly better outcomes when surgery was based on DISE (p < 0.001). In patients with mild OSA (AHI < 16.7), DISE conferred no additional benefit over AEMM. DISE-based surgical planning improves outcomes in moderate-to-severe OSA, while AEMM remains adequate for mild OSA cases. Disease severity should guide the choice of preoperative airway assessment method.

papers.title: Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome: a critical narrative review of modern concepts and unani perspectives.
papers.abstract: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a chronic, disabling, multisystem illness characterized by persistent fatigue, post-exertional malaise/post-exertional symptom exacerbation (PEM/PESE), unrefreshing sleep, and cognitive impairment. Classical Unani medicine does not recognize ME/CFS as a distinct disease entity. However, its descriptions of fatigue (I'yā), particularly I'yā Dhātī (spontaneous fatigue), provide a basis for examining parallels with ME/CFS. To examine I'yā Dhātī (spontaneous fatigue) and its three simple subtypes (I'yā Qarūḥī, I'yā Tamaddudī, and I'yā Waramī) and compare them qualitatively with contemporary ME/CFS, including areas of similarity and discordance. This critical narrative review used structured searches of PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science. Eight primary Unani sources were examined: Al-Qānūn fi al-Ṭibb, Kulliyāt al-Qānūn, Kitāb al-Ḥāwī, Kitāb al-Murshid, Kitāb al-Manṣūrī, Dhakhīrah-i Khwārazm Shāhī, Kitāb al-Kulliyāt, and Al-Mukhtārāt fi al-Ṭibb. The three subtypes were compared using predefined qualitative domains based on contemporary ME/CFS features and classical descriptions. I'yā Tamaddudī (distensive fatigue) showed the greatest phenomenological overlap with ME/CFS, particularly spontaneous fatigue, generalized heaviness, sleep disturbances, mental dullness, reduced functional capacity, and diffuse somatic manifestations. However, no clearly documented classical equivalent of delayed PEM/PESE was identified, representing a major area of discordance. I'yā Tamaddudī (distensive fatigue) showed the greatest phenomenological/conceptual overlap with ME/CFS among the subtypes examined. This represents a historical and interpretative correspondence, not biological, diagnostic, or therapeutic equivalence. Independent operationalization and prospective evaluation are required before its clinical or biological relevance can be established.

papers.title: Syndromic Autism in Helsmoortel-Van der Aa Syndrome: From Clinical Suspicion to Genetic Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Syndromic autism refers to autism spectrum disorder (ASD) occurring as part of an identifiable genetic syndrome. Helsmoortel-Van der Aa syndrome (HVDAS/ADNP syndrome) is a rare autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in the ADNP gene. We report a 10-year-old boy with ASD and intellectual disability who exhibited delayed motor and language development, characteristic facial dysmorphism, early tooth eruption, endocrine abnormalities, electroencephalography (EEG) abnormalities, and urogenital findings. Following unremarkable karyotyping and chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA), whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic de novo frameshift variant, c.1239_1240del, p.(Gln414Valfs*25) in ADNP. This case emphasizes the importance of considering a syndromic etiology in children with ASD accompanied by developmental delay, dysmorphic features, neurological findings, or multisystem involvement, and supports comprehensive genetic evaluation when first-tier testing is unrevealing.

papers.title: A scoping literature review of factors associated with burnout among student pharmacists in the United States.
papers.abstract: Burnout is an increasing challenge among student pharmacists. Individual studies have examined burnout among student pharmacists; however, faculty and college administrators lack a consolidated understanding of the educational, personal, and contextual factors associated with burnout. This scoping literature review explored factors associated with burnout among student pharmacists in the United States. For this scoping literature review, MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, and PsycINFO were searched for English-language studies published between January 2000 and February 2026. Records were deduplicated in EndNote and Covidence. Eligible studies reported factors associated with burnout or related outcomes, including emotional exhaustion, anxiety, depression, and poor well-being. Quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies were included. Two independent reviewers screened studies, assessed full texts, and extracted data, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Reporting followed PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Eleven studies met the inclusion criteria from 2893 screened records. Most were published since 2020, used observational survey designs, and included students from one or more United States colleges of pharmacy. Validated burnout measures, primarily the Maslach Burnout Inventory and Oldenburg Burnout Inventory, were commonly used. Burnout was associated with intrinsic program factors (year in program, workload, competitive culture, campus assignment), extrinsic factors (co-curricular activities, employment, career planning), and individual factors (sex, marital status, sleep, nutrition, resilience, lack of time). One randomized trial found a mindfulness application reduced burnout after six weeks, although longer-term effects were mixed. Burnout requires systemic curricular reform, integrated wellness initiatives, and longitudinal, multi-institutional research to improve student well-being and reduce burnout.

papers.title: Possible Epstein-Barr virus-associated central nervous system involvement with reversible electroencephalographic abnormalities in a child: a case report.
papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated central nervous system (CNS) involvement in children is uncommon and may present with nonspecific neurological symptoms. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) may remain normal, making diagnosis challenging. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) has emerged as a useful diagnostic tool, although positive EBV results require careful clinical interpretation. A previously healthy 5-year-old boy presented with fever (38.5 ℃), headache, dizziness, and nausea for 3 days without seizures, altered consciousness, focal neurological deficits, or ataxia. Laboratory tests showed leukocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers. Brain MRI was unremarkable. CSF examination revealed an opening pressure of 120 mmH2O and mild pleocytosis (13×106/L, 100% mononuclear cells), with normal glucose and protein levels. CSF tNGS detected EBV (24,002 sequence reads; estimated pathogen concentration <103 copies/mL), while no other pathogens were identified and autoimmune encephalitis antibodies were negative. Serum EBV DNA was positive, and EBV serology demonstrated viral capsid antigen (VCA)-IgM positivity during the acute phase followed by VCA-IgG seroconversion during recovery. Electroencephalography (EEG) showed sharp and sharp-slow wave discharges in the left parietal, occipital, and posterior temporal regions despite normal MRI. The patient received intravenous ganciclovir (10 mg/kg twice daily for 2 weeks) and empirical ceftriaxone for 4 days. Clinical symptoms resolved completely, follow-up EEG normalized, and no neurological sequelae were observed at 1-month follow-up. This case highlights that possible EBV-associated CNS involvement may occur in children despite normal brain MRI and only mild CSF abnormalities. The combination of CSF tNGS, dynamic EBV serology, EEG findings, exclusion of alternative etiologies, and clinical follow-up may facilitate diagnosis. Because EBV detected in CSF does not necessarily indicate causation, results should always be interpreted in the context of the overall clinical presentation.

papers.title: Dual-pathway processing of AI-generated Chinese ink painting: evidence from eye-tracking, EEG, and artistic expertise.
papers.abstract: AI-driven generative art is changing the scope of artistic creation, but the principles behind its aesthetics and the perception of its outcomes remain relatively unexplored, especially concerning culturally specific art forms. The present study investigates how viewers cognitively, affectively, and evaluatively process AI-generated Chinese ink paintings, and whether artistic expertise moderates these responses. We introduce the concept of expressive expansion as a viewer-perceived psychological effect - the tendency for AI-generated ink works to elicit higher ratings of expressiveness and dynamic tension than traditional counterparts - and examine its neural and behavioral correlates using a multimodal paradigm. Stimuli generated using a pre-trained Stable Diffusion architecture were assessed according to three aesthetic metrics along with traditional and digital non-AI artworks by 120 respondents equally split into professional artists and non-artists. Multidimensional measurement based on eye-tracking, semantic differential rating, and EEG showed that, under blind viewing conditions, AI-generated stimuli yielded significantly greater scan-path entropy and beta band suppression than traditional and digital non-AI works, suggesting that they engaged broader attentional exploration and increased attentional engagement as indexed by implicit behavioral and neural measures. Professional and non-professional evaluators agreed on expressiveness evaluation scores but differed considerably in their cultural authenticity perception, suggesting a dissociation between aesthetic appeal and cultural validity. These findings are consistent with a dual-pathway interpretive framework in which perceptual-affective and cultural-evaluative responses can dissociate as a function of artistic expertise - an account advanced as consistent with the observed dissociation rather than as a mechanism established by the present data - and contribute to the emerging empirical literature on audience responses to AI-generated art in culturally specific domains. All conclusions are restricted to the selected stimulus sets under the present experimental conditions. The source code, LoRA model weights, and experimental datasets will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/15100376058/ink-painting-ai-expressive-expansion (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20540420).
